newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big seller of OEX August 890 puts.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big seller of OEX August 890 puts.

text.p: Major U.S. stock index options were mostly quiet Monday with the highlight being heavy volume in the S&P 100 August 890 puts.
The August 890 puts traded nearly 13,000 contracts by about 1215 CDT/1715 GMT.
Traders said a U.S. institution sold about 10,000 of those contracts at 4-5/8.
"They crossed about half," one OEX trader said. "I believe they had gotten long those puts last week."
The spot OEX was up 0.95 at 924.21 after falling to a session low of 919.87. It climbed as high as 927.18.
"It's been quiet," the OEX trader said. "There was a little business going on this morning until (the index) rallied back."
Overall, OEX put volume outpaced call volume by 15,363 contracts by midday, a rate some analysts said was bullish.
Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, called the index put/call ratio "very encouraging for the bulls."
He said the market is on pact to trade about 700,000 more index puts than index calls during the current expiration cycle.
The intraday reading was similar in S&P 500 .SPX options, where put volume was 26,734 compared to call volume of 10,121.

Traders said despite the market's choppy action -- the bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI fell to an early session low of 8,134 before recovering most of that gain -- index option volatilities were holding steady.
"Volatility isn't moving too much," one index trader said, noting that Friday's selloff helped firm up most volatilities.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's (CBOE) volatility index, was down 0.42, or 1.75 percent, at 23.78.
The VIX, which is calculated off certain front-month OEX contracts, traded between 23.44 and 24.52. On Friday, it climbed to 25.27 before settling down to close at 24.20, up 0.45 on the session.
"Everything's holding steady from Friday," the OEX trader said.
In addition to the August 890 puts, other active OEX options included the August 920 put, the August 925 call and the August 960 call.
In the SPX, activity was led by the August 900 and 920 puts, which traded 4,545 and 3,120 contracts, respectively.
